newsitem.title: USA: Most Americans approve of U.S. air strikes on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Most Americans approve of U.S. air strikes on Iraq.

text.p: Sixty-nine percent of Americans approve of President Bill Clinton's decision to launch missile attacks in Iraq, a new TIME Magazine/CNN poll of likely voters released on Friday said.
The poll of 2,080 adult Americans, including 1,683 registered voters, was conducted by Yankelovich Partners on Sept. 4-5 and has a sampling error of 2.2 percentage points.

The poll found that 52 percent of Americans viewed the president as a strong leader in foreign policy matters and 65 percent said Clinton was right to use military force when other countries decided not to join in.

U.S. cruise missiles severely damaged Iraqi air defences this week, destroying or damaging up to 11 of 15 targets, the Pentagon said on Friday in its first public assessment of raids on southern Iraq.

The satellite-guided missiles were fired from over 500 miles (800 km) away in two strikes against air defence targets in southern Iraq to punish President Saddam Hussein for a military drive into a Western-protected "safe haven" for Kurds in northern Iraq.

Fifty-three of the people polled said Clinton made the decision to promote U.S. goals in Iraq and the Gulf, while 35 percent viewed the missile attacks as an election tactic. Twelve percent said they were unsure.
The TIME/CNN poll showed Clinton leading his Republican challenger Bob Dole, 52 percent to 38 percent, with six percent pledging their support for Reform Party candidate Ross Perot.
Forty-six percent of the people polled said they opposed sending manned aircraft into Iraq, while 44 percent said they would support the action.
Sixty-five percent favour using military force to remove Saddam from power, but 60 percent oppose the use of U.S. ground troops in Iraq, according to the poll.
